Header.CaseTitle: Beacon Manufacturing Ltd v Alliance Insurance Plc
Header.AppealFrom: High Court of Justice, King's Bench Division

Counsel.Lead: Robert Wilson KC; Sarah Roberts (instructed by Slaughter and May)

SummaryOfPosition.Summary: The Respondent contends that the claim is excluded under the policy by reason of the Appellant's material non-disclosure and/or breach of warranty regarding fire safety systems.

FactsReliedOn.item: The proposal form specifically asked about previous fire incidents and the Appellant answered 'None'.
The Appellant had experienced two previous fires in 2018 and 2020, neither of which was disclosed.
The policy contained a warranty requiring maintenance of fire suppression systems to British Standards.
At the time of the fire, the sprinkler system had been partially decommissioned for maintenance.
Had the true position been disclosed, the Respondent would not have written the risk.

Contentions.item: The non-disclosure was of material facts that induced the contract.
The Respondent is entitled to avoid the policy for material non-disclosure.
Breach of the fire safety warranty discharged the Respondent's liability.
The claim is in any event exaggerated and not proven.

ReliefSought.item: Declaration that the policy is void ab initio
Alternatively, that there is no cover for the claim

AuthoritiesCited.Authority: Pan Atlantic Insurance Co Ltd v Pine Top Insurance Co Ltd [1995] 1 AC 501

OpposingArguments.item: The Appellant contends that there was breach of duty. The Respondent denies this and maintains that all obligations were fulfilled.
The Appellant argues causation is established. The Respondent contends that any loss was caused by intervening factors.

SecurityConsiderations.item: The standard of care applicable is that of a reasonably competent practitioner in the relevant field.
The burden of proof rests with the Appellant to establish breach and causation on the balance of probabilities.
